name: Warzone
label: Revelation
lede: Raybeez, a drummer Agnostic Front had let go, took over the mic of his side band, kept a Lower East Side crew around him and handed Revelation Records its catalog number one.

eras.title: Rat Poison, then the front of the stage
eras.text: Raymond "Raybeez" Barbieri, a Washington Heights kid and Navy veteran, lived in Lower East Side squats with Roger Miret and drummed on the first Agnostic Front record. The side band he started, first called Rat Poison, became his whole life once he stepped out from behind the kit.

years.h: Raybeez keeps time on Agnostic Front's United Blood
years.p: Raymond "Raybeez" Barbieri drums on [[Agnostic Front|40b8a690-94e4-4c82-ad0f-73f4b841e46a]]'s debut EP. The same year he starts a Lower East Side band called Rat Poison, soon renamed Warzone.
years.xp:
Raybeez met Roger Miret at a [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] show at Irving Plaza. The two became close friends and lived together in Lower East Side squats, including Apt. X and C-Squat.

Before Warzone settled, Raybeez also played in the short-lived Skinhead Youth with [[Todd Youth|5a277693-a8b6-4d34-b821-4d6b33a08f03]] on bass, Big Al (later of [[Cause for Alarm|1940001f-3270-4d87-9501-eb243d5f9f50]]) on guitar and Billy Psycho on drums.

years.h: Raybeez steps out from behind the kit
years.p: About two years in, Raybeez moves from drums to vocals. No Echo says Roger Miret told him to sing because he was a terrible drummer.
years.xp:
Bandcamp Daily puts it more bluntly: Raybeez made Warzone his main priority after Agnostic Front kicked him out for being too unstable.

From then on he was the one constant. Guitarists, bassists and drummers rotated through for fourteen years, among them Todd Youth, [[Walter Schreifels|9f350578-acdd-480e-8273-5eaf88842f1c]] and Miret himself on bass.

eras.title: Revelation's number one
eras.text: By 1986 Warzone had a crew around them, the Warzone Women included, and a sound Vice credits with leading NYHC's second, bigger wave. Then two kids starting a label heard the band might split and decided to get it on vinyl first.

years.h: CindiB and Bethany sing on the As One demo
years.p: The demo comes out as a Some Records tape, recorded at Don Fury's studio. Warzone Women CindiB and Bethany sing backing vocals on the title song, As One.
years.xp:
The Warzone Women formed in late 1985 or early 1986: twenty to thirty women from the scene who flyered, sold shirts, followed the band to Albany and cleared pits by locking hands and spinning. Vice called them non-groupie groupies.

Two of them, Alexa Poli and Gwyn McAllister, put out a joke fanzine around 1986 called Lifestyles of the Poor & Homeless.

yt: Morning Show: NYHC 1986 with Raybeez and Todd Youth
years.h: Raybeez and Todd Youth take NYHC to morning TV
years.p: A 1986 television segment on New York hardcore features Raybeez and guitarist [[Todd Youth|5a277693-a8b6-4d34-b821-4d6b33a08f03]]. Youth leaves Warzone around then for [[Murphy's Law|4a9fae02-7de0-4cb8-97d7-1fd790d9675e]].

years.h: Kids mosh in a Rockland County pool, and two men get arrested
years.p: Warzone and Nausea play a pool party at the family home of Warzone Woman Brooke Smith. Roger Miret and English Nick are arrested that day.

years.h: Lower East Side Crew becomes Revelation No. 1
years.p: Jordan Cooper and [[Ray Cappo|e8357f9d-f7f5-4858-a766-aef004bb38a6]] heard Warzone might break up and wanted the band on record. The 7" sells well enough to keep the new label going.
years.xp:
The first pressing was 1,000 black copies with light blue labels hand-drawn in black ink, some B-sides numbered 1 to 100. Forty-one came with white paper labels and a Warzone logo colored in with orange marker.

The 7" went through four pressings by 1989. Six orange copies of the second press came in an alternate sleeve of a lion attacking a horse, and 150 of the 300 clear fourth-press copies went to the band with no sleeves at all.

years.h: CBGB hosts the Lower East Side Crew release show
years.p: One of the Warzone Women remembered the sound as awful, and the band tearing the place up anyway.

years.h: WNYU puts Warzone on the air live
years.p: Warzone play a live session on New York's college station WNYU, later released as Live on WNYU.

years.h: The first album gets cut at Studio X in New Jersey
years.p: Raybeez, guitarists Paul and Jay Vento, bassist John "Omen" and drummer Lukie Luke record Don't Forget the Struggle, Don't Forget the Streets in Ridgewood with producer Fink.

eras.title: The cross on the cover
eras.text: Warzone's first album made its title track an NYHC anthem and put a symbol on the cover that people argued over. The next two records leaned toward hard rock, and the momentum of 1987 slipped.

q: Hardcore music is a movement, not a business.
years.h: Don't Forget the Struggle opens with Raybeez running late
years.p: The skit explains he's missing because he went to get the Warzone Women. The album runs about 25 minutes, out first on the band's own Fist Records and then on Caroline.
years.xp: The liner notes carried a line that summed up the band's attitude.
play: Don't Forget the Struggle, Don't Forget the Streets
Don't Forget the Struggle, Don't Forget the Streets

years.h: Some read the cover as an iron cross, and Raybeez says no
years.p: To some the cover of Don't Forget the Struggle looked like an iron cross, a touchy symbol for a skinhead band. Raybeez answered that American hardcore skinheads stood for patriotism and unity, not racism.
years.xp: Warzone's Lower East Side crowd was mixed, and the band made clear that racist skins weren't welcome. The Warzone Women described Raybeez's whole message as unity across race, gender and money.

years.h: Open Your Eyes follows on Caroline
years.p: Warzone's second album comes out on Caroline. A 1994 Another Planet reissue pairs it with Don't Forget the Struggle.

years.h: The self-titled Warzone LP turns toward hard rock
years.p: No Echo calls the new direction unsuccessful.

eras.title: Raybeez rebuilds on Victory
eras.text: In the '90s Raybeez rebuilt Warzone on Victory Records, with Don Fury, Bad Brains' Dr. Know and label boss Tony Brummel behind the board. The run ended in September 1997, when he died at 35.

years.h: Four years after the last record, Live at CBGBs
years.p: Warzone's first release in four years is a live EP recorded at CBGB, the club where they'd celebrated their first 7".

years.h: Don Fury produces Old School to New School
years.p: A covers album that starts Warzone's stretch on Victory Records. Fury engineered a generation of NYHC records.

years.h: Raybeez sits down with the Droid Rage webzine
years.p: The March 15 conversation with Mike becomes Warzone's last interview, but it isn't published until May 2016, twenty years later.

years.h: Dr. Know of Bad Brains produces The Sound of Revolution
years.p: [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]] guitarist Dr. Know produces Warzone's album for Victory.

years.h: Tony Brummel produces Fight for Justice
years.p: Victory Records founder Tony Brummel runs the board for the last Warzone album released in Raybeez's lifetime.

years.cap: Raybeez fronting Warzone at QE2, Albany, N.Y., January 10, 1997
years.h: Raybeez dies at 35, and Warzone ends with him
years.p: Raymond "Raybeez" Barbieri dies of complications from pneumonia while being treated at a Veterans Health Administration facility. According to Wikipedia, the illness damaged his liver.
years.xp:
An "R.I.P Ray" sign went up at CBGB. Victory Records dedicated its releases to him for more than a year, and benefit shows raised money for the youth causes he supported.

Those causes were part of the band: Raybeez spoke up for drug-free living and for runaway and abused kids, and he was the only member who was in Warzone from start to finish.

eras.title: Tompkins Square remembers him
eras.text: Warzone never carried on without Raybeez. Victory gathered the '90s records, Revelation brought the first album back, and twenty years after his death the Lower East Side threw him a free show in the park.

years.h: The Victory Years gathers the '90s records
years.p: Victory Records rounds up Warzone's later work on one partial discography.

years.h: Revelation puts the first album back out as REV 163
years.p: Warzone's debut returns with its original artwork, 29 years after the band's 7" launched the label.

years.cap: Raybeez tribute show, Tompkins Square Park, New York, 2017
yt: Raybeez tribute, full set, Tompkins Square Park
years.h: Twenty years on, Tompkins Square Park turns out for Raybeez
years.p: [[Murphy's Law|4a9fae02-7de0-4cb8-97d7-1fd790d9675e]], Agnostic Front, [[Gorilla Biscuits|0320a32e-b781-40df-bf48-5cb5ee842762]] and [[Madball|c9e0a0f5-9f53-4247-a52d-a3f29d975e17]] play in his memory.

years.h: Todd Youth, ex-Warzone guitarist, dies at 47
years.p: [[Todd Youth|5a277693-a8b6-4d34-b821-4d6b33a08f03]], who left Warzone around 1986 and went on to Murphy's Law, D Generation and [[Danzig|8925a01a-8608-411d-a90b-f3a52d061208]], dies at 47. Wikipedia gives no cause.
